name: Action Construction Equipment Ltd
title: Action Construction Equipment Ltd - 532762 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 total income rose about 19% to INR836 crore and EBITDA grew 19.66% to INR170.58 crore, with management guiding to a full-year growth number only in late September.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as its best-ever first quarter on revenue and profit, with standalone EBITDA margin at 20.40%, up 12 bps YoY. Cranes, Construction Equipment and Metal Handling revenue rose about 22% to INR738.37 crore, while Agri Equipment brought in INR42.67 crore. Gross margin contracted roughly 140 bps YoY on commodity inflation, which management says it is offsetting through roughly 10% cumulative price increases taken since January. Management declined to give a full-year growth target until September, citing demand unpredictability and price resistance during the monsoon lean season.

segments.name: Cranes, Construction Equipment and Metal Handling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR738.37 crore, up about 22% YoY; volumes up 17.25% and segment margin INR134.09 crore, up 24.35% YoY. Backhoe loaders and construction equipment run at about 150-160 units per quarter.

segments.name: Agri Equipment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR42.67 crore with margin of INR4.34 crore in Q1 FY27 (about 10% margin); management expects agri at about 6-7% of FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Defense
segments.commentary: About 5% of Q1 revenue; management expects 5-6% of FY27 revenue and says it should exceed the INR200 crore order target. Rough terrain forklift manufacturing started this quarter; a repeat order above INR100 crore is expected in 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 3% of Q1 revenue, held back by shipping disruption; management expects 6-7% or more for FY27, with Middle East orders pending since March.

guidance_outlook: No full-year revenue growth number until late September 2026; management says growth is expected but will not quantify it now.
Q2 FY27 expected to be similar to Q1 and better than Q2 FY26, based on the 40-45% first-half revenue split.
Management is not targeting margin expansion; the aim is to hold EBITDA margin at the FY26 level of a little over 15% (operating EBITDA) through Q2 and possibly Q3.
Commodity inflation expected at 11-12% in costing, with about 10% already priced in and roughly 2% more price action possible depending on August-September conditions.
Total FY27 capex of INR200-250 crore: about INR130-140 crore for land takeover, INR40-50 crore for Plant 9, and INR50-60 crore for upgrades, automation and maintenance.
KATO JV is to start by end-July 2026, with first revenue in Q3 FY27 and meaningful revenue only from FY28.
Tower crane capacity expansion decision deferred to September; start in October or deferred by about six months.
Plant 9 (defense and special machines) expected functional by end-December 2026 with turnover capacity near INR500 crore.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR200-250 crore, including about INR130-140 crore for taking over land contracted 1.5-2 years ago.
Plant 9 at INR40-50 crore, dedicated to defense manufacturing and special machines, with functional target end-December 2026 (Q3 end, early Q4).
Tower crane capacity has reached about 1,000 cranes per year after rearrangements and a rented small factory nearby; a new plant 4-5 km away is planned, with the start decision in September.
Plant 9 will use the last large land parcel in the existing complex (about 100 acres), so the complex will be largely full afterwards.

KATO JV total investment of about INR200 crore: INR100 crore cash from KATO and INR100 crore in kind from ACE (machine models, technology, infrastructure). Upgraded KATO-standard Indian models expected from Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Demand was strong until May-June; rains have slowed buying, and management expects Q2 to be similar to Q1.
Price increases: about 1-1.5% in January, 3-4% in March, and 5-6% in June (still being implemented), for about 10% in total, with the last 4-5% still rolling through as of the call.

Commodity inflation: steel up nearly 20%, with tyres, belts, rubber and plastics also rising. Q1 commodity inflation was about 5-6% in costing, with 7-8% flowing through to prices; the rest spills into Q2.

Pick and carry mix: management expects Hydra to new-generation (NG) volumes to return to about 60:40 this year from the roughly 40:60 seen last year, and eventually around 50:50. Hydra volumes have risen in the last 3-4 months after the retail segment's skepticism about BS V electronic engines eased.
Competitive intensity described as unchanged. The main challenge is inflation and customers' ability to absorb price increases.
Backhoe loaders are being tested in 3-4 specific pockets with a finance company tie-up. Management expects them to become the fastest-growing segment, with full clarity by July-August.

qa_highlights.question: How much did defense and export contribute to Q1 revenue, and what is the FY27 visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Export was about 3% and defense about 5% of Q1 revenue. For FY27, management expects exports of 6-7% or more and defense of 5-6%, for a total of about 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the KATO JV's progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Formalities are complete and the JV should be functional by end-July. Revenue starts in Q3, and meaningful revenue comes from FY28, with localization targeted at 50-60% for export models in about two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give a FY27 growth target, and how is the market shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says growth is expected from Hydra cranes, construction equipment, forklifts, tower cranes, inflation-led pricing and defense orders. It will give a full-year number by late September, citing unpredictable demand and resistance to repeated price rises.

qa_highlights.question: How do gross margins look, and will margins expand from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin fell about 140 bps YoY on steel, rubber and freight. Management says it is not targeting margin expansion, only recovering costs, and aims to hold EBITDA margin above 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the tower crane capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Plans are ready, but the start was deferred from April because of the war. A decision on timing comes in September, with a plant 4-5 km from the existing site.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and revenue potential of Plant 9?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant 9 costs INR40-50 crore and is aimed at defense and special machines, with turnover capacity of about INR500 crore. Total FY27 capex is INR200-250 crore including land.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation of 11-12% against about 10% of price increases booked. Any shortfall or resistance from customers would hit margins.
Monsoon-related demand: management said a deficient monsoon could cut Tier 2 and rural demand by 5-10%, with the effect visible in Q3.
Export shipments to Middle East (Saudi Arabia) were delayed, with orders pending since March; shipping costs remain high.
Supply chain: engine and casting shortages were faced in the last month, with recovery expected in July.
Anti-dumping duty on Chinese cranes: no notification yet, and the Finance Ministry reportedly did not implement the DGTR recommendation.
Tower crane expansion and capex timing depend on September decision; FY27 guidance pending until late September.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating execution and the best-ever Q1, but cautious on forward numbers: management declined to quantify full-year growth or margin upside, citing inflation, price resistance and unpredictable demand. It was candid about commodity pressure and the expected price lag.
key_quotes: Against this backdrop, our company registered its best -ever Q1 performance with continued focus on disciplined execution, operational excellence and maintaining a healthy balance between growth and profitability.
So we see, obviously, there is a lot of resistance. And this is coupled at a time when the market is at its leanest because of rains.
